column1: # #152: the ONE set of URL-canonicalisation cases both platforms must agree on.
# Windows (windows/taburl.js) and Android (TabUrl.kt) both de-duplicate tabs by
# comparing canonical keys. They reconcile against each other through the sync
# service, so a disagreement does not stay theoretical — it produces duplicate
# tabs on one device and not the other, which is exactly #152.
# Read by BOTH windows/taburl.test.js and TabUrlTest.kt. Add a case here and it
# must pass on both or one of them goes red.
# Format:  <input url> TAB <expected canonical key>      ('' means empty string)
# Plain text rather than JSON on purpose: the JVM unit-test classpath has only a
# stubbed android.jar, so org.json throws there, and a dependency-free format
# keeps the fixture readable from both sides.
# --- scheme and default ports are not significant --------------------------
# --- the query string IS significant: it is how apps identify pages ---------
# --- fragments: a route counts, an anchor does not -------------------------
# --- the Charles Schwab case that opened #152 ------------------------------
# An auth bounce changes the query string every time. These are DIFFERENT keys,
# which is correct — canonicalisation alone does not fix Schwab. The adoption
# guard must ALSO not treat every new URL as a new tab; see #152's cap and the
# --- non-http is returned untouched, so internal pages never merge ---------
# --- junk compares literally rather than being guessed at -----------------
